arxiv-2110-11949.title: Hydrodynamic superradiance in wave-mediated cooperative tunneling
arxiv-2110-11949.creator: K. Papatryfonos, M. Ruelle ∗, C. Bourdiol ∗, A. Nachbin, J.W.M. Bush, M. Labousse
arxiv-2110-11949.description: Abstract Superradiance and subradiance occur in quantum optics when the emission rate of photons from multiple atoms is enhanced and diminished, respectively, owing to interaction between neighboring atoms. We here demonstrate a classical analog thereof in a theoretical model of droplets walking on a vibrating bath.

arxiv-2304-04689.title: There and back again: Solar cycle effects in future measurements of low-energy atmospheric neutrinos Preprint: FERMILAB-PUB-23-143-T, CERN-TH-2023-056, MI-HEE-800
arxiv-2304-04689.creator: Kevin J. Kelly, Pedro A. N. Machado, Nityasa Mishra, Louis E. Strigari, Yi Zhuang
arxiv-2304-04689.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Kevin J. Kelly, Pedro A. N. Machado, Nityasa Mishra, Louis E. Strigari, Yi Zhuang. We study the impact of time-dependent solar cycles in the atmospheric neutrino rate at DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande (HK), focusing in particular on the flux below 1 GeV.

arxiv-2307-02460.title: Performance Scaling via Optimal Transport: Enabling Data Selection from Partially Revealed Sources
arxiv-2307-02460.creator: Feiyang KangBradley Department of ECEVirginia Tech fyk@vt.edu, Hoang Anh JustBradley Department of ECEVirginia Tech just@vt.edu Anit Kumar SahuAlexa AIAmazon anit.sahu@gmail.com Ruoxi JiaBradley Department of ECEVirginia Tech ruoxijia@vt.edu
arxiv-2307-02460.description: Abstract Traditionally, data selection has been studied in settings where all samples from prospective sources are fully revealed to a machine learning developer. However, in practical data exchange scenarios, data providers often reveal only a limited subset of samples before an acquisition decision is made.

arxiv-2310-10449.title: Text Summarization Using Large Language Models: A Comparative Study of MPT-7b-instruct, Falcon-7b-instruct, and OpenAI Chat-GPT Models
arxiv-2310-10449.creator: Lochan Basyal, Mihir Sanghvi
arxiv-2310-10449.description: Abstract Text summarization is a critical Natural Language Processing (NLP) task with applications ranging from information retrieval to content generation. Leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) has shown remarkable promise in enhancing summarization techniques. This paper embarks on an exploration of text summarization with a diverse set of LLMs, including MPT-7b-instruct, falcon-7b-instruct, and OpenAI ChatGPT text-davinci-003 models.

arxiv-2311-14440.title: Fluctuation Relations at Large Scales in Three-Dimensional Hydrodynamic Turbulence
arxiv-2311-14440.creator: Alexandros Alexakis, Sergio Chibbaro, Guillaume Michel
arxiv-2311-14440.description: Abstract It has long been conjectured that, in three dimensional turbulence, velocity modes at scales larger than the forcing scale follow equilibrium dynamics. Recent numerical and experimental evidence show that such modes share the same mean energy and therefore support this claim, but equilibrium dynamics does not reduce to equipartition of energy.

arxiv-2401-00157.title: Theory of Metastability in Discrete-Time Open Quantum Dynamics
arxiv-2401-00157.creator: Yuan-De Jin, Chu-Dan Qiu, Wen-Long Ma
arxiv-2401-00157.description: Abstract Metastability in open system dynamics describes the phenomena of initial relaxation to long-lived metastable states before decaying to the asymptotic stable states. It has been predicted in continuous-time stochastic dynamics of both classical and quantum systems. Here we present a general theory of metastability in discrete-time open quantum dynamics, described by sequential quantum channels.

arxiv-2503-16971.title: Nofl: A Precise Immix CCS: Software and its engineering Garbage collection CCS: Software and its engineering Runtime environments
arxiv-2503-16971.creator: Andy Wingo
arxiv-2503-16971.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Andy Wingo. Can a memory manager be built with fast bump-pointer allocation, single-pass heap tracing, and a low upper bound on memory overhead? The Immix collector answered in the affirmative for the first two, but the granularity at which it reclaims memory means that in the worst case a tiny object can keep two 128-byte lines of memory from being re-used for allocation.

arxiv-2504-12327.title: Word Embeddings Track Social Group Changes Across 70 Years in China
arxiv-2504-12327.creator: Yuxi Ma 1 , ✉ {}^{1,\,\textrm{{\char 0\relax}}} Yongqian Peng 1,2 Yixin Zhu 1 , ✉ {}^{1,\,\textrm{{\char 0\relax}}} yxma@stu.pku.edu.cn yqpeng@stu.pku.edu.cn yixin.zhu@pku.edu.cn 1 Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Peking University 2 Yuanpei College, Peking University ✉ corresponding authors
arxiv-2504-12327.description: Abstract Language encodes societal beliefs about social groups through word patterns. While computational methods like word embeddings enable quantitative analysis of these patterns, studies have primarily examined gradual shifts in Western contexts. We present the first large-scale computational analysis of Chinese state-controlled media (1950-2019) to examine how revolutionary social transformations are reflected in official linguistic representations of social groups.

arxiv-2505-06873.title: Ultraslow growth of domains in a random-field system with correlated disorder
arxiv-2505-06873.description: Abstract We study domain growth kinetics in a random-field system in the presence of a spatially correlated disorder h i ​ ( r → ) h_{i}(\vec{r}) after an instantaneous quench at a finite temperature T T from a random initial state corresponding to T = ∞ T=\infty .

arxiv-2505-14733.title: The Energy Cost of Reasoning: Analyzing Energy Usage in LLMs with Test-time Compute
arxiv-2505-14733.creator: Yunho Jin, Gu-Yeon Wei, David Brooks
arxiv-2505-14733.description: Abstract Scaling large language models (LLMs) has driven significant advancements, yet it faces diminishing returns and escalating energy demands. This work explores how test-time compute (TTC) can serve as an energy-efficient complement to conventional scaling strategies by allocating additional computational resources at inference time rather than during training.

britannica-1911-bathory-sigismund.title: Báthory, Sigismund (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-bathory-sigismund.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-bathory-sigismund.description: Article 'Báthory, Sigismund' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 3), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. following the advice of his favourite councillor Alfonso Carillo, departed from the traditional policy of Transylvania in its best days (when friendly relations with the Porte were maintained as a matter of course, in order to counterpoise the ever hostile influence of the house of Habsburg), and joined the league of Christian princes against the Turk.

plos-pone-0010386.title: Therapeutic Value of Zinc Supplementation in Acute and Persistent Diarrhea: A Systematic Review
plos-pone-0010386.creator: Archana Patel, Manju Mamtani, Michael J. Dibley et al.
plos-pone-0010386.description: PLOS ONE research article. For over a decade, the importance of zinc in the treatment of acute and persistent diarrhea has been recognized. In spite of recently published reviews, there remain several unanswered questions about the role of zinc supplementation in childhood diarrhea in the developing countr

pmc-10652126.title: Accuracy of Preoperative 3D vs 2D Digital Templating for Cementless Total Hip Arthroplasty Using a Direct Anterior Approach
pmc-10652126.creator: Thomas Aubert, Giacomo Galanzino, Philippe Gerard, Vincent Le Strat, Guillaume Rigoulot, Luc Lhotellier
pmc-10652126.description: BackgroundAn important aspect of preoperative planning for total hip arthroplasty is templating. Although two-dimensional (2D) templating remains the gold standard, computerized tomography (CT)-based three-dimensional (3D) templating is a novel preoperative planning technique. This study aims to compare the accuracy of a 2D and 3D plan using an anterior approach for the placement of the same uncemented prosthesis.

pmc-10730341.title: Non-linear associations of maternal pre-pregnancy body mass index with risk of stillbirth, infant, and neonatal mortality in over 28 million births in the USA: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-10730341.creator: Hannah V Thornton, Rosie P Cornish, Deborah A Lawlor
pmc-10730341.description: SummaryBackgroundHigher maternal pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI) has been associated with higher risk of stillbirth, infant and neonatal mortality. Studies exploring underweight have varied in their conclusions. Our aim was to examine the risk of stillbirth, infant and neonatal mortality across the BMI distribution and establish a likely healthy BMI range.

pmc-11595268.title: Calcium Transport Activity of UV/H2O2-Degraded Fucoidans and Their Structural Characterization
pmc-11595268.creator: Biyang Zhu, Jiacheng Wang, Lijun You, Lianzhu Lin, Kuncheng Lin, Kseniya Hileuskaya, Paola Laurienzo
pmc-11595268.description: Calcium-chelated polysaccharides have been increasingly considered as promising calcium supplements. In this study, degraded fucoidans (DFs) with different molecular weights (Mws) were prepared after UV/H2O2 treatment; their calcium-chelating capacities and intestinal absorption properties were also investigated. The results showed that the calcium-chelating capacities of DFs were improved with a decrease in Mw.

pmc-11643363.title: Advancements in Adenine Nucleotides Extraction and Quantification from a Single Drop of Human Blood
pmc-11643363.creator: Ivana Popović, Lucija Dončević, Renata Biba, Karla Košpić, Maja Barbalić, Mija Marinković, Mario Cindrić, Victoria Samanidou, Irene Panderi
pmc-11643363.description: Adenine nucleotides (ANs)—adenosine 5′-triphosphate (ATP), adenosine 5′-diphosphate (ADP), and adenosine 5′-monophosphate (AMP)—are essential for energy transfer and the supply of countless processes within cellular metabolism. Their concentrations can be expressed as adenylate energy charge (AEC), a measure of cellular metabolic energy that directly correlates with the homeostasis of the organism.

pmc-11656989.title: The interactivity and independence of Recovery challenges and coping strategies for ICU survivors and their caregivers: a systematic review and Meta-synthesis
pmc-11656989.creator: Zeyi Zhang, Longshan Yang, Heng Cao
pmc-11656989.description: BackgroundThe post-ICU home recovery period requires patients and caregivers to confront recovery challenges and adopt coping strategies as a family dyad, necessitating effective dyadic interaction patterns. Existing qualitative research shows that the dyads face interactive or independent challenges and employs varying coping strategies, which may include strong communication or, conversely, avoidance.

pmc-11713747.title: Head‐to‐head evaluation of leading blood tests for amyloid pathology
pmc-11713747.creator: Kellen K Petersen, Suzanne E Schindler, Duygu Tosun, Benjamin A Saef, Leslie M Shaw, Yan Li, Ziad S Saad, Gallen Triana‐Baltzer, Michael Baratta, Erin G Rosenbaugh, Anthony W Bannon, William Z Potter, the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), and the Foundation for the National Institu
pmc-11713747.description: BackgroundBlood tests that accurately determine the presence of amyloid pathology are critically needed. Compared to amyloid PET and CSF tests, blood tests are less expensive, less invasive, more accessible, and highly scalable. The Foundation for the National Institutes of Health (FNIH) Biomarkers Consortium evaluated the accuracies of leading AD blood tests in classifying amyloid PET status.

pmc-12626822.title: A SHAP-interpretable machine learning framework for predicting delayed discharge in ambulatory total knee arthroplasty: comparative validation of 14 models
pmc-12626822.creator: Jiabin Feng, Fei Yuan, Pan Luo, Rang Chen, Binghu Jiang, Bin Li, Fang Luo, Li Sun, Bo Li
pmc-12626822.description: BackgroundThe rising global demand for total knee arthroplasty (TKA) has accelerated the shift toward ambulatory surgery, aimed at same-day or next-day discharge. However, significant variability in discharge protocols and high rates of delayed discharge in unselected patients challenge its widespread implementation. This study develops an interpretable machine learning framework to preemptively identify risk factors for delayed discharge in ambulatory TKA.

pmc-12652627.title: Facile Preparation of Glass Fiber Wool/MTMS Aerogels with Improved Thermal Insulation and Safety
pmc-12652627.creator: Yong Ren, Huanlin Zhang, Xingwei Jiang, Miao Liu, Zhi Li, Duckjong Kim
pmc-12652627.description: With the continuous increase in global energy consumption and the escalating severity of climate change, the development of high-performance thermal insulation materials is crucial for reducing energy waste and carbon emissions. In this work, a facile method was proposed to prepare thermal-insulating glass fiber wool/methyltrimethoxysilane aerogel (GFWA) composites through vacuum-assisted impregnation.

pmc-12655709.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Pharmaceutical Formulation and Dosage Calculations
pmc-12655709.creator: Sameer Joshi, Sandeep Sheth, Thierry Vandamme, Adam Pacławski, Jakub Szlęk
pmc-12655709.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reforming pharmaceutical sciences by renovating traditional drug formulation and dosage calculation approaches. This review provides a comprehensive overview of how AI technologies, such as machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and natural language processing (NLP), are currently being used in pharmaceutical calculations to improve accuracy, efficiency, and personalization.

pmc-13064416.title: Causative Role for a BRCA2 Germline Pathogenic Variant in External Auditory Canal Squamous Cell Carcinoma
pmc-13064416.creator: José Camacho‐Valenzuela, Dylan Pelletier, Paz Polak, Lili Fu, Nancy Hamel, Carla Daniela Robles‐Espinoza, William D Foulkes
pmc-13064416.description: External auditory canal squamous cell carcinoma (EACSCC) is rare, affecting 1.6 in a million individuals. We report a case of EACSCC in a 66‐year‐old woman carrying a heterozygous BRCA2 germline pathogenic variant (GPV) (c.8537_8538del), with prior history of breast cancer. Tumor copy‐number analysis showed loss of heterozygosity at the BRCA2 locus.

pmc-13085642.title: Disrupting stigma associated with dementia and dance through documentary film
pmc-13085642.creator: Pia Kontos, Alisa Grigorovich, Romeo Colobong, Devin Sodums, Jon Parr Vijinski, Rosanne Aleong, Rachel J Bar
pmc-13085642.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundDance is a powerful means to reduce stigma associated with dementia by promoting, preserving, and sustaining human flourishing. However, dance is rarely adopted for this purpose in the context of dementia care; as with other art programming, dance is primarily adopted in dementia care to achieve individual therapeutic or functional needs and outcomes rather than to support access to the art form itself and social engagement through co-creativity.

pmc-13418583.title: Physicochemical and Microbial Regulation Inhibit Rice Mercury Accumulation in the Karst Region with High Geological Background
pmc-13418583.creator: Yanxin Hu, Zhengcheng Song, Lu Qiao, Xinyu Liang, Shaochen Yang, Junyao Yan, Langfei Wei, Jinjuan Li, Ping Li
pmc-13418583.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Methylmercury (MeHg) accumulation in rice is a major source of human MeHg exposure in some inland areas, yet the mechanism controlling mercury (Hg) accumulation in high geological background (HGB) regions remains poorly understood. Here, a field-scale remediation experiment was conducted in a karst HGB region of Guizhou, China, using a synergistic strategy combining selenium foliar spraying and calcium oxide-based soil conditioner. The combined treatment reduced total Hg and MeHg concentrations in rice grains by 63.0% and 80.0%, respectively.

pmc-13541836.title: Correction: Low carbohydrate availability reduces power output at the moderate-to-heavy transition, impairs efficiency, and increases median power frequency during cycling in females
pmc-13541836.creator: Evana Main, SangHoon Yoon, Samuel L James, Kimberley M Mellor, Matthew J Brick, Warren B Leigh, Ed Maunder
pmc-13541836.description: nd Figure 2. The Figure 1 should have appeared as shown below. Schematic overview of the randomised crossover study design. pmc-13722222.title: Comparative analysis of adenosine deaminase (ADA) and polymerase chain reaction (PCR/GeneXpert) for diagnosing pleural and peritoneal tuberculosis
pmc-13722222.creator: Aparnna Unnikrishnan Nair, Sanjana Laishram, Shoraf Pascal, Muskan Joshi, Gayathri Pramil Menon, Lakshmi Murugesan, Nithila Sivakumar, Lakshiya Ramamoorthy, Ruchi Kothari, Roshan Prasad, A Prashanth
pmc-13722222.description: Context:Tuberculosis (Tb) is one the most prevalent diseases, with a huge disease burden in various developing countries, such as India. Given the large burden of TB cases, the proportion of extrapulmonary tuberculosis (EPTB) cases has also risen in recent years. The diagnosis of EPTB poses a significant challenge, owing to its atypical characteristics.
